A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAPS research work. All 30 pages of v1 and 37 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original FFHQ and ImageNet experiments, supplemented by synthetic posterior-sampling experiments and ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original restoration experiments and adds original MRI, text-conditioned restoration, discrete MNIST and sampler-comparison results.

M1.justification: The core decoupled annealing framework remains, but v2 adds HMC and Metropolis–Hastings samplers, an alternative diffusion-score conditional estimate, and a discrete-diffusion algorithm using a Hamming-distance approximation. It also introduces text-conditioned sampling and reports fully latent updates where v1 used a pixel/latent hybrid.

E1.justification: V2 adds fastMRI knee reconstruction and binarized MNIST inpainting/XOR tasks, extending evaluation into medical imaging and categorical data. It also tests prompt-controlled reconstruction of natural images. The original FFHQ, ImageNet and synthetic coverage remains.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds DCDP, FPS-SMC, DiffPIR and HIO in applicable comparisons, removes PnP-ADMM, and drops DDRM from random inpainting. Figure 6 additionally evaluates DPnP. New MRI and discrete comparisons include ScoreMRI/CSGM and SVDD-PM/best-of-N, respectively.

E3.justification: V2 adds SSIM and FID to the main benchmark metrics and changes reported LatentDAPS budgets, including 100 to 50 Langevin iterations. New protocols include Stable Diffusion evaluation at measurement noise 0.01, MRI subsampling factors 4 and 8, and sampler ablations using five tuning images and ten test images. These reported changes do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New studies compare Gaussian versus diffusion-score approximation (Table 3), HMC/Langevin/Metropolis–Hastings sampling (Table 9), and runtime versus quality (Figure 6). V2 adds prompt-control and qualitative ODE-step analyses. Earlier noise, scheduling, synthetic-posterior and oversampling analyses largely remain after relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions retain across-image standard deviations for nonlinear benchmarks, best-of-four phase-retrieval sampling, fixed mask/kernel seeds and 100 independent synthetic samples. Added uncertainty-bearing results extend existing reporting practices; no new repeated-run or statistical-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive MRI, Stable Diffusion, discrete-data, design-choice and SSIM/FID results. Retained results also change: FFHQ phase-retrieval DAPS is revised from 30.72 PSNR/0.121 LPIPS in v1 Table 2 to 30.63/0.139 in v2 Table 1. Several DPS, DDRM and LatentDAPS scores change, with LatentDAPS revisions accompanying changed settings.

T1.justification: The original marginal-distribution propositions and proofs are retained. V2 adds a conditional-score derivation, Hamiltonian and Metropolis–Hastings formulations, and discrete forward/reverse Markov-chain definitions with a Hamming-distance approximation. The discrete formulation has an internal inconsistency: Algorithm 3 uses the opposite exponent sign from Equation 26.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the contributions to MRI, large text-conditioned models and categorical inverse problems. It also narrows the claimed FFHQ phase-retrieval advantage from 9.12 dB to 1.98 dB with the expanded comparisons. The central claim about decoupling enabling larger corrective transitions remains.

C2.justification: V2 develops substantive accuracy–efficiency and gradient-access explanations for approximation and sampler choices. Appendix I explains the ODE-step LPIPS/PSNR tradeoff through increased image detail. V1's explicit conclusion warnings about irrecoverable approximation error and expensive forward models are omitted, while its older appendix limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands implementation information through task-specific sampler settings, learning-rate decay, HMC parameters, Stable Diffusion versions, guidance scale and prompts. It adds MRI preprocessing and new baseline configurations. The GitHub code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands its research context through newer posterior solvers, MCMC methods, discrete diffusion and large conditional models. Section 3.4 adds an explicit MAP-versus-posterior distinction involving ReSample, DiffPIR and DCDP. PnP-ADMM references disappear; DiffPIR itself was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Much of the original exposition remains verbatim. V2 revises the introduction and experimental narrative, divides the method explanation into additional subsections, and relocates Algorithm 1 and the NFE/oversampling discussions. Most additional prose documents new scientific content rather than extensively rewriting retained material.

P2.justification: V2 switches the main text to two columns and consolidates v1 Tables 1–4 into an expanded task-by-method table. Figure 1 is rebuilt, and runtime, text-control, MRI and ODE-detail displays are added. Existing appendix galleries and analyses are mostly retained, resized, reordered or relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for DAPS's practical choices and generality. Tables 3 and 9 directly test approximations and samplers, while stronger baselines and MRI evaluation address gaps in v1's comparative and application evidence. These gains outweigh localized defects: the phase-retrieval introduction/Table 1 mismatch and Algorithm 3/Equation 26 sign inconsistency reduce reporting precision and reproducibility of the discrete extension.
